scenes.say: The test is {sensitivity} accurate. You tested positive. You're probably fine. Here's the math doctors get wrong.
Most people, even many doctors, guess about ninety percent. It's far lower.
Take {n} people. Only {prevalence} actually have the disease.

scenes.say: {tp} sick people test positive. But {fp} healthy people test positive too.
So a positive result means only a {ppv} chance you're sick.
When a condition is rare, false alarms from the healthy majority drown out the few real cases.
Before trusting a signal, ask: is this thing rare or common to begin with?
